title: Why Work with THREE? It’s Where Science, Entrepreneurship and Human Connection Meet
description: THREE and CEO Daniel Picou connect three elements: people, platform, and purpose to give entrepreneurs something meaningful to share.
author: Three
html:
THREE International was built around a simple but ambitious idea: business can be a platform for helping people redefine what is possible. Since launching in 2023, THREE has brought together science-driven wellness innovation, entrepreneurship, and a culture of human connection to create something larger than a traditional wellness company. Its achievement is not simply the products it has developed or the business opportunity it offers but the community it is building around both.

At the heart of THREE’s corporate excellence is a commitment to science. The company has made product quality, efficacy, safety, and bioavailability central to its identity, supported by a Scientific Advisory Board composed of medical and scientific experts. Under Chief Scientific Officer Dr. Dan Gubler, THREE has focused on advanced delivery technologies and cellular absorption, creating products designed around how the body can effectively utilize nutrients. Its scientific approach is reinforced by a portfolio of products listed in the Prescriber’s Digital Reference (PDR), demonstrating the company’s commitment to building credibility around its formulations.

But innovation at THREE is not limited to what is inside a bottle. The company is also innovating in how people can participate in business. THREE’s entrepreneurial platform is designed to give individuals the opportunity to build something of their own while providing a community, education, and leadership environment intended to support long-term development. This reflects CEO Daniel Picou’s belief that people are capable of far more than they realize when given the right leadership and environment.

Picou describes his leadership philosophy this way: “At its best, this business is not transactional; it’s transformational.” That philosophy is visible in the culture THREE is creating. Rather than defining success solely by short-term transactions, THREE emphasizes relationships, personal development, leadership, and the creation of sustainable entrepreneurial opportunities.

The response from the community reflects that culture. One THREE leader, Patricia K. Clements, commented, “Love working with so many wonderful leaders!” Another, Lee Ann Seeley, wrote, “You are an amazing CEO, and I am so proud to be part of THREE.” These comments illustrate something difficult to capture in conventional business metrics: people feel connected to the organization and to one another. Public commentary from THREE leaders has similarly emphasized Picou’s willingness to develop people, create opportunities for growth, and treat individuals with respect regardless of their position in the organization.

That sense of community is central to THREE’s leadership achievement. Picou is not simply building a company around a product line; he is building an environment in which entrepreneurs can develop alongside the organization. The model connects three elements: people, platform, and purpose, creating an ecosystem in which scientific innovation gives entrepreneurs something meaningful to share, while the entrepreneurial community gives the company a human connection to the people it ultimately serves. THREE itself describes this as delivering greater health to people, a dynamic platform for entrepreneurship and greater purpose through community.

THREE’s achievement, therefore, is both corporate and human. It demonstrates that a company can pursue rigorous product innovation while investing in relationships, leadership development and entrepreneurial potential. It is building a community designed not only to grow but to help the people within it grow as well.

That combination of science, entrepreneurship, and human connection is what makes THREE International worthy of recognition.

title: GLP THREE™: A Natural Approach to GLP-1 Support
description: Discover how GLP THREE offers natural, nutrition-based support for GLP-1 pathways, appetite awareness, and metabolic wellness.
author: Three
html:
GLP-1 has become one of the most talked-about topics in conversations around appetite, healthy weight management, and metabolic health. But maintaining a healthy weight has never been just about limiting your caloric intake. Metabolism is the sum of numerous processes happening inside your body all at once, all working together to influence how you function day to day.

So where does GLP-1 fit into that picture and why does it matter so much for hunger and fullness? Let's break it down.

What Is GLP-1 and What Does It Have To Do With Food Noise?

GLP-1 is a natural peptide hormone in the body that interacts with the GLP-1 receptor, playing a role in appetite awareness and several metabolic processes along the way.

That connection to appetite is exactly why GLP-1 comes up so often in discussions about “food noise.” If you haven’t heard the term before, Dr. Dan Gubler, Chief Science Officer at THREE International, describes food noise as those persistent, looping thoughts about food that can show up throughout the day, regardless of whether you are actually hungry. Appetite and satiety signaling (the cues that tell your brain you’ve had enough to eat) can have a real influence on that mental chatter and on your eating behavior overall.

It’s important to note that supporting GLP-1-related pathways through nutrition is not the same as taking a pharmaceutical GLP-1 receptor agonist. These are two different categories, formulated for different purposes, and they aren’t interchangeable. Nutritional support is about working alongside your body’s existing processes, not replacing them with a prescription medication.

How Does GLP THREE Support Metabolic Wellness?

GLP THREE is built around MBC-267 (Metabolic Boost Complex-267), a natural peptide complex sourced from salmon and mushrooms. As Dr. Dan explains, MBC-267 is formulated around its relationship to the GLP-1 receptor, giving GLP THREE its foundation.

Alongside MBC-267, GLP THREE includes:

  • Panax Ginseng
  • Saffron
  • Hops
  • Peppermint

Getting the right ingredients into a formula is only half the equation, though. THREE’s cellular absorption approach is designed to help MBC-267 actually reach where it needs to go, guiding the complex through the GI tract and cellular membrane so it can get to work as intended. It’s one of the key things that sets GLP THREE apart from other GLP-1 supplements on the market alongside its natural, food-sourced profile.

For best results, take ¾ of a dropper about 30 minutes before a meal, or as desired.

For a closer look at what’s inside GLP THREE, check out What Makes GLP THREE a Clean, Natural Metabolic Support Formula?

Support Your Metabolic Wellness with GLP THREE

GLP THREE is a daily metabolic wellness product formulated to support appetite awareness, healthy weight management, and overall metabolic health. It’s built on a foundation of natural peptides, MBC-267, and THREE’s cellular absorption technology, giving you a nutritional approach to GLP-1 support that’s grounded in real formulation science.

If quieting the food noise and supporting your body’s natural processes sound like goals worth pursuing, GLP THREE was designed with exactly that in mind.

title: The Future of Women’s Wellness Is Metabolic, Not Cosmetic
description: There’s more to metabolic wellness for women than counting calories and tracking changes in weight. Dr. Dan Gubler, Chief Science Officer, breaks it all down, here.
author: Dr. Dan Gubler, Chief Science Officer, THREE International
html:
Metabolic health is quickly becoming the central framework for understanding women’s long-term wellness and performance. The focus in women’s health is moving from how women’s bodies look or isolated wellness concerns, to how the body is governed by energy regulation, hormonal signaling, and cellular efficiency.

Dr. Dan Gubler, Chief Science Officer for THREE International, shares,“As a scientist, I believe the future of wellness lies in helping people better understand these interconnected biological systems rather than chasing fragmented solutions.The most exciting innovations happening right now are not necessarily about creating stronger stimulants or more aggressive interventions. They are about supporting the body more intelligently.”

Why Metabolic Health Is Reshaping Women’s Wellness

Metabolic wellness is more than counting calories and tracking changes in weight. True metabolic wellness for women is about positively influencing energy production, increasing cognitive performance, supporting healthy hormone signalling, and increasing metabolic resilience.

The outcomes women want often stem from molecular health meaning how nutrients, compounds, and biochemical pathways interact at the cellular level to produce energy, regulate, and support overall physiological balance.

“We now have the data to prove that stress affects metabolism. Sleep affects hormones. Gut health influences mood and cognitive performance. When one area becomes dysregulated, the effects often spread much further than people realize.” Dr. Gubler says.

While many wellness products still approach these challenges through short-term solutions, real health is built gradually through consistency, nutrient support, movement, sleep, and sustainable daily habits.

The Future of Women’s Wellness Is Smarter Science

Consumers are becoming much more informed, and that will always be a good thing. Women especially are asking smarter questions about ingredients, clinical validation, sourcing, and how products actually function inside the body at a biological systems level. The future of wellness will belong to companies willing to prioritize education, transparency, and science over hype.

With the shift in demand for science-backed solutions, products like THREE International's GLP THREE provide the long-term metabolic support that women’s health needs. title: The Power of Plant Ingredients in Immune Support
description: The lifestyle basics matter — but plant compounds offer immune support that diet and vitamins alone can't replicate. Learn how phytonutrients, botanical extracts, and natural plant ingredients support your body's immune defenses from the inside out.
author: Three
html:
When a health journey begins, most people start on the same traditional path. Eat the right foods, try to get the right amount of sleep, manage your stress to the best of your ability, and move your body every day. All of that advice is correct, and it's incredibly important as it’s the foundational base that health is built on. Once healthy lifestyle fundamentals are in place, consider adding in plant-based compounds as an additional layer of support as a way to work through mechanisms that lifestyle and diet alone aren’t able to replicate.

For those who have accomplished the health basics and built a foundation that can be built upon, plant nutrition offers natural immune support and a way to further enhance your lifestyle and overall wellness.

The Foundation First , What Actually Supports Health of the Immune System

The foundation for good health has been clear for a long time. Consume a nutrient-dense diet; maintaining gut health is key, with 70-80% of immune activity occurring in the gut; getting between seven and nine hours of sleep each night, managing stress in a healthy way, and participating in a moderate exercise program are all keys to living well. This foundation mirrors what most Google searches and health institutions tell you about maintaining good health and supporting the health of your immune system.

When it comes to your nutrition, the first lines of natural immune support are whole foods with vitamin C, vitamin A, and omega-3s. With your nutrition and basic health foundations in place, including plant compounds offers additional tools that food and lifestyle alone may not fully provide.

Why Plant Compounds Are a Different Category of Immune Support

Phytonutrients are incredible. These compounds are produced by plants specifically for their own support. Research has found how these compounds interact with human biology. Unlike vitamins and minerals, phytonutrients work through additional mechanisms, including receptor modulation, antioxidant cascade support, microbiome influences.

While vitamins and minerals give the immune system the foundational materials needed for immunity support, plant compounds give it additional intelligence. While vitamins and supplements come with a use-only-as-needed directive, botanical compounds are much more closely linked to concentrated food problems, which has them working with the body’s existing biology rather than replacing something that may be missing. While traditional medical systems across cultures have relied on plant compounds to support immune system health for thousands of years, modern research is just now beginning to map the mechanisms behind these observations.

The Plant Compounds Most Studied for Immune Support

If you’ve ever shopped for plant compounds to supplement your immune support, you’ve most likely seen elderberry and mushroom immune support at the front of the shelf!

Mushrooms are the most substantive botanical in the immune support category. Beta-glucans, which are found in reishi, shiitake, maitake, and turkey tail, are among the most studied phytonutrients for immune support. They support both innate and adaptive immune responses. THREE has long studied plant nutrition and mushroom benefits, and they are also an ingredient in Imúne's formula.

Elderberry is also one of the most popular and well-recognized botanical immune ingredients. Elderberry is known for containing anthocyanins, the pigments behind its deep purple color, and these pigments have been studied for both antioxidant and immune-supporting properties. They are widely visible in the supplement market and are known as a credibility anchor for health-conscious consumers.

Aloe vera has a great deal of value beyond its skincare reputation. Aloe vera contains acemannan, a polysaccharide that has been studied for immune-supporting properties. Aloe vera is also included in Imúne's formula for its internal immune-support benefits.

Adaptogens and stress-resilient plants are known as the cortisol PAA. Have you ever wondered how high cortisol affects the immune system? Stress suppresses immune function. Adaptogenic plants like ashwagandha and astragalus have been studied for their role in supporting the body's stress response, which has downstream effects on immune health. This is all part of a holistic plant-based approach.

Zinc-rich plant sources are another great option as they serve as a bridge between botanical and mineral support. Seeds, legumes, and nuts are all highly valuable in assisting with plant-based immune support.

The Gut-Immune System Connection , Where Plants Make a Meaningful Difference

Incredibly, 70% of immune activity originates from the gut. The gut microbiome houses and trains a significant portion of the immune system. title: Vitamins and Your Immune System
description: Discover the key immune support vitamins and minerals your body needs, how nutrient gaps affect immune health, and what to look for in a quality supplement.
author: Three
html:
Many people turn to immune support vitamins hoping to support their body's natural defenses, but few know which nutrients actually matter, or why. With countless products on the market promising immune support, it can be difficult to separate science-backed nutrition from marketing claims.

The reality is that your immune system depends on a specific group of vitamins and minerals to function properly. While a healthy diet remains the best source of these essential nutrients, nutritional gaps can occur due to age, lifestyle, dietary restrictions, stress, or other factors. In those cases, targeted supplementation may help support overall immune wellness.

In this guide, we'll explore the science behind the vitamins and minerals your immune system relies on most, and how to choose a supplement designed to help support your body's natural defenses.

How Your Immune System Actually Uses Vitamins and Minerals

Your immune system isn't a single organ or an "on/off" switch. It's a complex network of cells, tissues, organs, and chemical messengers working together to recognize potential threats and help keep your body functioning normally.

This system operates through two primary lines of defense.

The innate immune system is your body's first responder. It reacts quickly to a wide range of potential threats using physical barriers like your skin and mucosal tissues, along with specialized immune cells that provide an immediate, non-specific response.

The adaptive immune system is more specialized. Rather than responding broadly, it identifies specific pathogens and develops targeted responses. This part of the immune system also creates immunological memory, allowing the body to recognize familiar threats more efficiently in the future.

Both systems require a continuous supply of essential nutrients to function effectively. Vitamins and minerals help support everything from the production of immune cells and signaling molecules to the maintenance of the tissues that act as your body's first line of defense. In fact, the immune system is one of the most nutritionally demanding systems in the body, constantly relying on micronutrients to carry out its normal functions.

It's also important to understand what immune support really means. The goal isn't to artificially "boost" your immune system. A stronger immune response isn't always better, balance is what matters. Instead, proper nutrition helps ensure your body has the nutrients it needs to support healthy immune function and maintain its natural defenses.

Because your body cannot produce some of these vitamins and minerals on its own, food remains the primary source. A diet rich in fruits, vegetables, whole grains, lean proteins, nuts, and seeds provides many of the nutrients your immune system depends on every day. However, dietary gaps can occur, and when they do, targeted supplementation may help fill those nutritional gaps and support overall immune health.

The Vitamins and Minerals Your Immune System Depends On Most

Research consistently points to a core group of nutrients as being especially important for healthy immune function. Each one plays a unique role in supporting your body's natural defenses.

Vitamin C

Vitamin C is perhaps the most well-known nutrient associated with immune health, and for good reason. It plays an essential role in the production and function of several types of white blood cells, including neutrophils and lymphocytes, which help your body recognize and respond to potential threats.

Unlike some vitamins, the body doesn't produce or store vitamin C in significant amounts. That means a consistent daily intake through food or supplementation is important for maintaining healthy levels.

Vitamin C also helps support the skin's natural barrier, one of your body's first lines of defense. By supporting both immune cell function and physical barriers, vitamin C contributes to multiple layers of your body's natural immune response.

Vitamin D

What makes vitamin D especially important is that vitamin D receptors are found on nearly every type of immune cell. Rather than supporting just one aspect of immunity, vitamin D helps support both the innate immune system, your body's immediate response, and the adaptive immune system, which develops targeted responses over time.

Ensuring adequate vitamin D intake through diet, sunlight exposure when appropriate, or supplementation may help support your body's natural immune defenses.

Zinc

Zinc is a trace mineral that plays a critical role in nearly every stage of immune function. It supports the development and communication of immune cells while also supporting the body's natural inflammatory response.

Zinc is particularly important for the thymus gland, where T-cells mature. These specialized immune cells are central to the adaptive immune system's natural function.

In addition to its role in immune cell support, zinc contributes to the body's natural antioxidant processes by supporting enzymes that help support the body's natural reaction to oxidative stress.

Vitamin A

Vitamin A is best known for supporting healthy vision, but it's equally important for maintaining the body's protective barriers. It helps support the health of the mucosal tissues that line the respiratory tract, digestive tract, and other areas.

Vitamin A also supports the development and function of several immune cell types, making it an important component of overall immune wellness.

B Vitamins (B6, B9, B12)

The B vitamins work together to support many of the processes that support the health of the immune system. Vitamins B6, B9 (folate), and B12 are all involved in DNA synthesis, healthy cell division, and the production of new immune cells. Ensuring adequate intake of these essential nutrients helps support the continuous renewal of immune cells your body depends on every day.

Selenium

Although selenium is needed only in small amounts, it plays an important role in supporting immune function. This trace mineral helps activate antioxidant enzymes that protect cells from oxidative stress while also supporting normal immune cell activity.

Selenium works alongside nutrients such as vitamin E and other antioxidants to help maintain the body's natural defense systems. While it may not receive as much attention as vitamin C, vitamin D, or zinc, selenium is consistently included in research examining the nutrients that contribute to healthy immune function.

Together, these vitamins and minerals form the nutritional foundation your immune system relies on every day. Maintaining adequate levels through a balanced diet, and using targeted supplementation when appropriate, can help support your body's natural ability to respond to everyday challenges.

Who Might Experience Nutrient Gaps?

Age, lifestyle, diet, stress, and even certain medications can all influence how well your body absorbs and utilizes the vitamins and minerals it depends on.

Recognizing these factors can help you make informed decisions about your diet and whether targeted immune support vitamins for adults may be appropriate as part of your overall wellness routine.

Adults Over 50

As we age, the body naturally becomes less efficient at absorbing certain nutrients. Vitamin B12 absorption often declines due to changes in stomach acid production, while vitamin D synthesis decreases because the skin becomes less effective at producing it from sunlight. Older adults may also have lower zinc levels.

Because these nutrients play important roles in maintaining healthy immune responses, adults over 50 may benefit from paying closer attention to their nutritional intake and discussing supplementation with a healthcare provider when appropriate.

Women

Women's nutritional needs change throughout life, making them more susceptible to certain vitamin and mineral deficiencies depending on factors such as menstruation, pregnancy, breastfeeding, diet, and overall lifestyle.

Meeting recommended daily nutrient needs is especially important during periods when the body's demands increase. Maintaining adequate levels of vitamins and minerals helps support not only overall wellness but also the normal function of the immune system.

Stress Levels

Stress can also influence your nutritional status.

Periods of ongoing physical or emotional stress may increase the body's use of nutrients such as vitamin C and zinc, making it more difficult to maintain optimal levels through diet alone. At the same time, stress can contribute to changes in appetite, food choices, and sleep habits, all of which may further impact nutrient intake.

Supporting your body's nutritional needs during times of prolonged stress can help maintain your natural immune defenses alongside healthy lifestyle habits like adequate sleep, regular physical activity, and stress management.

While proper nutrition is essential, it's only one part of supporting your body's natural immune defenses. Sleep, stress management, regular movement, and hydration all contribute to immune wellness.

Learn more in our companion article: Everyday Habits That Impact Health of the Immune System.

Those with Dietary Restrictions

Certain eating patterns can make it more challenging to obtain enough of specific vitamins and minerals.

For example:

  • Plant-based diets may provide limited amounts of vitamin B12 unless fortified foods or supplements are included.
  • Calorie-restricted diets may reduce overall intake of essential nutrients.
  • Highly selective or limited diets can leave gaps in zinc, selenium, and other important micronutrients.

A well-planned diet can certainly provide the nutrients your immune system needs, but when dietary variety is limited, targeted supplementation may help close nutritional gaps.

People Taking Certain Medications

Some commonly prescribed medications can affect how the body absorbs, stores, or utilizes specific nutrients over time. Depending on the medication, this may influence levels of vitamin B12, vitamin D, magnesium, or other essential nutrients involved in normal immune function.

If you take prescription medications on a long-term basis, it's a good idea to discuss your nutritional status with your healthcare provider before adding any dietary supplements. They can help determine whether additional nutrients may be appropriate for your individual needs.

People Using GLP-1 Medications or Following Intensive Dietary Programs

Individuals using GLP-1 medications or participating in intensive weight management programs may also want to pay closer attention to their nutrient intake. Rapid dietary changes, reduced appetite, or lower overall food consumption can make it more difficult to consistently meet daily vitamin and mineral requirements.

While these approaches can support broader health goals, maintaining adequate nutrition remains important. A balanced diet should always be the foundation, and targeted supplementation may help support nutrient intake when dietary changes make meeting those needs more challenging.

No matter which category you fall into, consult your healthcare provider. They can recommend appropriate testing and help determine the best approach for supporting your long-term health and immune wellness.

Do Immune Support Vitamins Actually Work?

It's a fair question, and one that's become increasingly common as headlines continue to question whether dietary supplements provide meaningful benefits.

The honest answer is that some immune support vitamins don't deliver the results people expect. But that doesn't necessarily mean the nutrients themselves are ineffective. In many cases, the issue lies in the formulation.

Some supplements contain only small amounts of key nutrients, while others use ingredient forms that are poorly absorbed during digestion. Without effective delivery, a significant portion of those vitamins and minerals may be broken down before they ever reach the cells that need them.

The science supporting individual nutrients like vitamin C, vitamin D, and zinc is well established. These essential nutrients have been extensively studied for their roles in supporting normal immune function, maintaining healthy immune cells, and helping the body's natural defenses operate as intended. The question isn't whether these nutrients matter, it's whether the supplement you're taking is designed to deliver them effectively.

This is where bioavailability becomes one of the most important factors to consider.

Bioavailability refers to how much of a nutrient is absorbed, enters circulation, and becomes available for use by the body. Two supplements may list similar ingredients on their labels, but if one uses more bioavailable forms or advanced delivery technology, your body may be able to utilize those nutrients more efficiently.

That's why it's important to look beyond ingredient lists and serving sizes alone. The form of each nutrient, how it's delivered, and how well it's absorbed all influence whether a supplement can effectively support your body's nutritional needs.

Ultimately, the conversation shouldn't be about whether vitamins work. Research continues to demonstrate the importance of nutrients like vitamin C, vitamin D, and zinc in maintaining healthy immune function. Instead, the more meaningful question is whether your supplement is formulated to help those nutrients reach the cells where they can support the health of the immune system.

When combined with a balanced diet and healthy lifestyle, choosing a supplement designed with both nutrient quality and bioavailability in mind can help you close nutritional gaps more effectively than simply selecting the product with the longest ingredient list.

What to Look for in an Immune Support Supplement

With so many products on the market, choosing the right immune support supplement can feel overwhelming. Eye-catching labels and long ingredient lists don't always tell the full story. Instead of focusing on the number of ingredients alone, it's important to evaluate how a formula is designed to support the health of the immune system.

Here are a few key factors to consider when comparing immune support vitamins.

Look for the Core Nutrients

A well-rounded immune support formula should include the vitamins and minerals most closely associated with healthy immune function.

At a minimum, look for a supplement that contains:

  • Vitamin C
  • Vitamin D
  • Zinc

These three nutrients have been extensively studied for their roles in supporting normal immune function and are widely recognized as foundational components of immune wellness.

Even better are formulas that also include complementary nutrients such as vitamin A, B vitamins, and selenium. Because each nutrient supports different aspects of the immune response, combining them can provide more comprehensive nutritional support than relying on a single ingredient alone.

Prioritize Bioavailability

The amount of a nutrient listed on the label is only part of the equation. Just as important is how much of that nutrient your body can actually absorb and utilize.

This is where bioavailability becomes essential.

The form of each vitamin and mineral, along with the delivery technology used in the supplement, can influence how effectively those nutrients survive digestion and become available to your cells. A thoughtfully formulated product focuses not only on what goes into the capsule, but also on helping those nutrients reach the places they're intended to support.

When comparing products, consider whether the manufacturer emphasizes cellular absorption and ingredient quality rather than simply promoting higher dosages.

Look Beyond Vitamins with Plant-Based Ingredients

While vitamins and minerals provide the nutritional foundation for immune health, plant-based ingredients can offer additional support.

Botanical ingredients such as mushrooms, aloe vera, and elderberry contain naturally occurring phytonutrients that complement traditional vitamins and minerals. Rather than replacing core nutrients like vitamin C or zinc, these ingredients add another layer of nutritional support that may help maintain overall immune wellness.

Consider Formulas That Address Quorum Sensing

Some advanced immune support formulas go beyond vitamins and botanicals by incorporating ingredients designed to help support the body's natural microbial balance.

One emerging area of research is quorum sensing, the process bacteria use to communicate and coordinate their activity. Certain plant-based compounds are formulated to help inhibit this communication, providing another way to support the body's natural defenses alongside traditional immune-supporting nutrients.

While this doesn't replace the role of vitamins and minerals, it represents an additional layer of support that sets some comprehensive formulas apart.

To learn more about this growing area of research, read our companion article: Quorum Sensing Explained for Immune Support

Choose a Clean Formula

If you're taking an immune support supplement every day, the quality of the entire formula matters , not just the active ingredients.

Look for products made without:

  • Artificial colors
  • Artificial flavors
  • Unnecessary fillers
  • Synthetic additives

A clean formulation helps ensure you're getting the nutrients you want without ingredients you may prefer to avoid.

Look for Clinically Informed Formulations

Finally, consider the company behind the supplement.

Brands that invest in scientific research, work with qualified advisors, and clearly explain why each ingredient is included often provide greater transparency than those relying solely on marketing claims.

Instead of asking, "Does this supplement contain vitamin C?" ask questions like:

  • Why were these ingredients selected?
  • Are they included in forms that support absorption?
  • Does the formula address multiple aspects of immune health?
  • Is there a clear scientific rationale behind the formulation?

Choosing an immune support supplement isn't about finding the product with the longest ingredient list, it's about selecting one that's thoughtfully formulated to help support your body's natural immune defenses through high-quality ingredients, effective delivery, and a comprehensive nutritional approach.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can vitamin deficiencies cause you to get sick more often?

Certain vitamin and mineral deficiencies may affect your body's ability to maintain normal immune function. Nutrients such as vitamin C, vitamin D, zinc, and vitamin A all play important roles in supporting healthy immune responses. When levels are consistently low, your natural immune defenses may not function as efficiently. Maintaining adequate nutrient intake through a balanced diet , and supplementing when appropriate , can help support overall immune wellness.

Do immune support vitamins actually work?

Research supporting nutrients like vitamin C, vitamin D, and zinc is well established. These vitamins and minerals have important roles in supporting healthy immune function. However, not all supplements are created equal. The quality of the ingredients, their bioavailability, and the delivery technology used all influence how effectively your body can absorb and utilize those nutrients. The question isn't simply whether immune support vitamins work, it's whether the formula is designed to deliver them where they're needed.

Is it better to get immune vitamins from food or supplements?

Food should always be the primary source of vitamins and minerals whenever possible. A balanced diet rich in fruits, vegetables, whole grains, lean proteins, nuts, and seeds provides a wide variety of nutrients that work together to support overall health. Supplements aren't intended to replace healthy eating, they're designed to help close nutritional gaps when diet alone doesn't provide adequate intake.

What is quorum sensing and why does it matter for immune support?

Quorum sensing is the process bacteria use to communicate with one another and coordinate certain behaviors. Some advanced immune support formulas include botanical ingredients that are formulated to help inhibit this communication, providing an additional way to support the body's natural defenses alongside essential vitamins and minerals. While research in this area continues to evolve, quorum sensing represents a unique approach that complements traditional nutritional support.

title: Antioxidant Supplement From A Cellular-Level Perspective
description: Discover how antioxidant supplements work at the cellular level and why bioavailability, liposomal delivery, and key antioxidants matter for cellular support.
author: Three
html:
Most people have seen the headlines claiming that antioxidant supplements don't work. In many cases, those studies are pointing out a real problem, but not necessarily with antioxidants themselves. The bigger issue is that many antioxidant compounds never make it to the cells where they're intended to work.

That's why looking at an antioxidant supplement from a cellular perspective matters. Delivery technology, ingredient form, and bioavailability often determine whether nutrients are absorbed or simply broken down before they can be utilized by the body.

A healthy diet rich in colorful fruits, vegetables, nuts, seeds, and whole grains remains the foundation of antioxidant intake. Supplements aren't meant to replace those foods, they're designed to support what good nutrition starts, particularly when modern lifestyles, aging, or dietary gaps make optimal intake more difficult.

In this guide, we'll explore how antioxidants work at the cellular level, why bioavailability is one of the most overlooked factors in supplement quality, and what to look for when choosing a formula designed to support cellular health.

What Antioxidants Do (At the Cellular Level)

Every day, your cells naturally produce molecules known as free radicals. These unstable molecules are generated during normal metabolism, exercise, environmental exposure, UV radiation, pollution, and even stress.

When free radicals outnumber the body's ability to neutralize them, oxidative stress occurs. Over time, oxidative stress may affect proteins, lipids, DNA, and other important cellular structures.

Fortunately, the body comes equipped with its own antioxidant defense system.

Natural antioxidants, including glutathione, enzymes like superoxide dismutase, and nutrients obtained through food, help neutralize free radicals before they cause excessive oxidative stress.

However, several factors can influence these natural defenses, including:

  • Aging
  • Environmental pollutants
  • High stress levels
  • Intense physical activity
  • Dietary limitations

That's why many people choose antioxidant vitamins and other supplemental antioxidants, to help support the body's natural protective systems when diet alone may not provide optimal intake.

Why Bioavailability Is the Real Issue With Antioxidant Supplements

Not all supplements are absorbed equally.

One of the most important factors determining whether an antioxidant supplement is worthwhile is bioavailability , the percentage of an ingredient that actually reaches circulation and becomes available for use by the body.

Many antioxidant compounds face significant challenges after they're swallowed.

Before nutrients can reach your cells, they must survive:

  • Stomach acid
  • Digestive enzymes
  • Breakdown within the gastrointestinal tract
  • Metabolism before entering circulation

As a result, some ingredients lose potency long before they reach the tissues they're intended to support.

This is why simply listing impressive ingredient amounts on a label doesn't necessarily translate into effective cellular absorption.

Liposomal and Polyphenol-Coated Delivery

To help improve absorption, some modern formulations use advanced delivery technologies.

Liposomal antioxidants are encapsulated within tiny phospholipid spheres that help protect sensitive ingredients during digestion. These phospholipids resemble portions of the body's own cell membranes, which may support efficient delivery.

Some formulas also utilize a polyphenol supplement complex. Polyphenols not only provide antioxidant activity of their own, but they may also help stabilize other antioxidant compounds and support their activity.

Rather than relying solely on larger ingredient doses, advanced delivery systems focus on helping nutrients reach the cells where they're intended to function.

Key Antioxidants That Work at the Cellular Level

Glutathione , The Body's Master Antioxidant

Glutathione is often called the body's master antioxidant because it plays a central role in maintaining the body's natural antioxidant network.

However, traditional glutathione supplements can be easily broken down during digestion.

That's why liposomal glutathione has gained attention. Liposomal delivery is designed to help protect glutathione through the digestive process and support absorption, making it one of today's most researched bioavailable antioxidants.

Resveratrol , Plant-Based Polyphenol Protection

Resveratrol is a naturally occurring polyphenol found in grapes, berries, and certain plants.

It has been widely studied for its role in helping support the body's response to oxidative stress and free radicals.

Resveratrol also works alongside other antioxidants rather than acting alone, making it a valuable component of a well-rounded antioxidant formula.

Food remains the best source of antioxidants. Fruits, vegetables, nuts, herbs, and whole grains provide a wide variety of naturally occurring antioxidant compounds. Cellular absorption refers to how effectively nutrients survive digestion, enter circulation, and become available for use by the body's cells. Better absorption means more of the active ingredient has the opportunity to support normal cellular function.

title: Why You’re Always Hungry (Even After Eating)
description: Discover why you are always hungry and how weight management supplements like GLP THREETM can help curb your hunger cravings.
author: Three
html:
You just finished a full meal. You pushed the plate away, maybe even felt satisfied, and then, twenty minutes later, you’re rummaging through the pantry again, looking for a snack. Sound Familiar?

If you’re constantly battling hunger even after eating, you’re not alone. For people working hard to manage their weight or make more mindful food choices, persistent hunger can feel like a wall you just can’t get past. It’s frustrating, it’s demoralizing, and it has nothing to do with willpower.

The real reason you can’t stop feeling hungry is rooted in biology, specifically, in the way your body’s hunger and fullness signals communicate with your brain. Understanding what’s happening under the hood is the first step to doing something about it.

The Science Behind Why You Can’t Stop Feeling Hungry

Your sense of hunger isn’t random. It’s governed by a complex system of hormones that send signals back and forth between your gut, your body, and your brain. When this system is working the way it should, you feel hungry before meals, eat, feel full, and stop. When something disrupts that cycle, hunger signals can stay elevated long after you’ve eaten, and your brain never quite gets the message that it’s time to stop.

Here are the key players involved:

Ghrelin, The Hunger Hormone Ghrelin is the hormone responsible for telling your brain it’s time to eat. Levels rise before a meal and, in a well-regulated system, fall after you’ve eaten. But for many people, ghrelin doesn’t drop the way it should after a meal, especially after eating foods that don’t trigger adequate fullness responses. The result is that gnawing “still hungry” feeling that shows up far too soon after eating.

Leptin, The Fullness Hormone Leptin is produced by fat cells and signals the brain that the body has had enough food. Think of it as the “you can stop now” message. The issue? Over time, particularly when diets are high in processed foods and added sugars, the brain can become less responsive to leptin’s signal. When the brain stops reading that fullness cue clearly, overeating becomes almost inevitable, not because of bad habits, but because the signal simply isn’t getting through.

Metabolic Signaling Hormones, Beyond ghrelin and leptin, the gut releases a network of metabolic signaling hormones after eating that help communicate fullness to the brain and support healthy metabolic balance. When digestion is moving too quickly, or when food choices don’t trigger an adequate hormonal response, these messages can arrive late, weakly, or not at all, leaving the brain still waiting for confirmation that a meal has been eaten

Several everyday factors can interfere with the body’s hunger hormone signaling, including:

  • Ultra-processed foods and high-sugar diets, which can override natural satiety responses and promote ongoing cravings
  • Poor sleep, which is closely tied to ghrelin elevation and leptin reduction. Even one night of inadequate sleep can shift your hunger hormones noticeably
  • Chronic stress, which triggers a hormonal response that can increase appetite and drive cravings for high-calorie, high-sugar foods.
  • A sedentary lifestyle, which over time can contribute to metabolic imbalance and reduce the body’s sensitivity to fullness signals.

What You Can Do to Reset Your Hunger Signals Naturally

The good news: Lifestyle choices have a meaningful impact on how well your body reads and responds to hunger and fullness cues. Here are practical steps you can take to start working with your biology instead of against it.

1. Eat whole foods with protein, fiber, and healthy fats

Whole, minimally processed foods tend to trigger more complete hormonal responses after eating. Protein is particularly powerful: it takes longer to digest and supports more sustained satiety signals. Fiber slows the movement of food through the digestive tract, giving fullness hormones more time to do their job. Healthy fats contribute to meal satisfaction and help keep cravings quieter between meals. Building meals around these three pillars is one of the most effective ways to support your body’s natural hunger regulation.

2. Reduce highly processed foods

Highly processed foods are engineered to be hyper-palatable, and they often bypass the body’s normal fullness signaling. They digest quickly, spike and crash blood sugar, and tend to leave you hungry again faster than whole-food alternatives. Gradually swapping out processed options for whole-food choices can make a significant difference in how satisfied you feel after eating.

3. Prioritize sleep

Sleep is one of the most underrated factors in managing hunger. Even modest sleep deprivation can meaningfully shift hunger hormone levels, causing ghrelin to rise and leptin to fall: a combination that makes overeating far more likely the following day. Aiming for consistent, quality sleep is one of the best habits you can build for managing your appetite naturally.

4. Manage stress

Chronic stress keeps the body in a state of hormonal activation that can directly influence appetite and cravings, particularly for sweet, salty, or high-fat foods. Building stress management practices into your routine, whether through movement, breathwork, time in nature, or whatever works best for you, supports a more balanced hormonal environment overall.

5. Consider saffron

Saffron is one of the most well-researched botanicals when it comes to appetite and mood support. Its active compounds, safranal and crocin, have been recognized in traditional wellness practices for their ability to support a sense of well-being and satisfaction (both of which play a meaningful role in managing the emotional side of hunger and cravings). Saffron extract is increasingly found in natural metabolic support supplements for exactly this reason.

If you’re looking for a supplement specifically formulated to help support feelings of fullness and healthy hunger management, it's worth looking for one with saffron in the formula.

title: How to Curb Cravings Naturally
description: Cravings aren’t a willpower problem, they’re a biology problem. Discover 7 natural tips to reduce cravings and appetite, plus a clean botanical support with GLP THREE.
author: Three
html:
If you’ve ever found yourself raiding the pantry an hour after dinner or reaching for something sweet mid-afternoon despite your best intentions, you’re not alone. More importantly, you’re not lacking willpower.

Cravings are a biology story, not a character flaw. Your body is constantly sending and receiving signals about hunger, fullness, and energy. When these signals get scrambled by stress, poor sleep, skipped meals, or an unbalanced diet, cravings tend to get louder.

The good news? There are practical, natural ways to work with your biology instead of against it. Here are seven strategies to help you manage cravings and feel fuller longer.

7 Natural Ways to Curb Cravings and Feel Fuller Longer

Getting a handle on cravings doesn’t require extreme dieting or suffering your way through the afternoon. Small, consistent changes to your routine can make a meaningful difference in how hungry and satisfied you feel throughout the day.

1. Eat more protein at every meal

Protein is the most satiating macronutrient, meaning it helps you feel full and stay full longer than carbohydrates or fats alone. If cravings tend to hit hard between meals, take a look at your protein intake first. Great sources of protein include eggs, greek yogurt, chicken, fish, legumes, cottage cheese, and nuts. Aim to include at least one source of protein at every meal.

2. Don’t skip meals (especially breakfast)

It can be tempting to skip a meal in an effort to eat less overall, but this often backfires. Going too long without eating can cause hunger hormones to spike, making cravings more intense and harder to manage by the time your next meal rolls around. Regular, balanced meals help keep those signals steady throughout the day.

3. Slow down and chew thoroughly

It takes about 20 minutes for fullness signals to travel from your stomach to your brain, which means eating quickly can lead you to consume more than you actually need before your body has a chance to register satisfaction. Slowing down, putting your fork down between bites, and chewing thoroughly are simple habits that can meaningfully impact how full you feel after eating.

4. Stay hydrated and drink water before meals

Thirst signals can closely mimic hunger signals, which means that what feels like a craving is sometimes just your body asking for water. Drinking a glass of water before meals and staying consistently hydrated throughout the day is one of the easiest and most overlooked tools for managing appetite naturally.

5. Prioritize fiber-rich foods

Fiber slows digestion, which means food stays in your stomach longer and fullness lasts longer too. Vegetables, fruits, legumes, oats, and whole grains are all excellent sources. If your meals tend to be low in fiber, adding even one fiber-rich food per meal can make a noticeable difference in how long you stay satisfied.

6. Manage stress and prioritize sleep

When you’re stressed or sleep-deprived, cortisol levels rise. Elevated cortisol is strongly associated with cravings for high-sugar, high-fat comfort foods. This isn’t a lack of discipline; it’s a physiological response. Building in stress-management practices like movement, time outdoors, or journaling can help support more balanced appetite signals day to day.

7. Consider natural botanical support

Sometimes lifestyle habits alone need a little backup. Saffron, in particular, has a long history of use in traditional wellness practices and is studied for its role in supporting mood and curbing emotional eating. If you’re looking for a clean, natural supplement to complement the habits above, this is where GLP THREETM comes in.

title: The Overlooked Hormone Behind Metabolic Health

html:
Most people trying to support their health or manage their weight zero in on two things: calories and macros. What often gets overlooked is the role hormones play in how your body processes food, regulates energy, and signals when it's had enough.

Hormones act as chemical messengers in your body, telling different communication systems what to do and when. When it comes to metabolism, there’s one messenger in particular that plays a surprisingly central role in how you feel after a meal, how your body handles energy, and whether your metabolism is working the way it should.

What is the Metabolic Hormone and What Does It Do?

Your body naturally produces a group of hormones specifically designed to regulate how you eat and how you use energy. One of the most important of these is a naturally occurring hormone your gut releases in response to food. In plain terms, here’s what this hormone is designed to do:

Signal your brain that you’re full

After you eat, this hormone communicates with receptors in your brain to register that you’ve had enough. It’s part of the reason a satisfying meal leaves you feeling content rather than immediately wanting more.

Support healthy blood sugar balance

This hormone plays a role in how your body responds to the food you’ve just eaten, helping to support blood sugar levels in a normal, balanced way.

Regulate how your body uses energy

Beyond just the post-meal window, this hormone is involved in broader metabolic signaling, essentially helping your body decide how to allocate and use the energy it takes in.

When this hormone is functioning well, and its signals are getting through clearly, your body has a better shot at supporting the kind of metabolic balance most of us are trying to achieve.

Why Metabolic Hormone Levels Can Decline

If you’ve ever felt like you’re hungry again an hour after eating, find yourself dealing with persistent cravings, or your energy seems to crash in the middle of the day, it may have something to do with how well your body’s metabolic signaling is working.

When the body’s metabolic hormone signaling isn’t functioning well, the body may struggle to maintain healthy metabolic balance. Several factors can affect the body’s natural hormone signaling:

  • Diet Quality: Diets high in processed foods and refined sugars and low in fiber don’t provide the body with the raw materials it needs to support hormone function. Over time, these patterns may affect how well metabolic signals are sent and received.
  • Sedentary Lifestyle: Regular movement supports the body’s metabolic systems in ways that go beyond burning calories. When physical activity is consistently low, the systems that regulate energy and hunger can become less efficient.
  • Aging & Genetics: Even people who eat well and stay active may notice that metabolic function feels different as they get older. Hormone production and receptor sensitivity naturally shift with age, and genetics influence where you start and how quickly those shifts happen.

The encouraging part: there are natural ways to support this process. What you eat, how you move, how well you sleep, and the supplements you choose can all play a role in supporting the body’s natural hormone signaling pathways.

author: Three
html:
Many people start considering a full body cleanse when their routine feels a bit off, energy is low, or they feel mentally or physically overloaded. These physical signs suggest that your body might benefit from a full-body cleanse reset. If you’re feeling the need to change, it’s tempting to jump right in; however, we urge caution. The timing of your cleanse plays a key role in how effective it can be. It’s best to pick a time in your life and schedule that allows for consistency and focus.

Your ability to stay focused and consistent will impact the results of your cleanse. It’s not wise, for example, to start a cleanse on the first day of vacation or during the week of your daughter’s wedding. These life events will make it harder for you to focus and stay consistent. Pick a time in your life and schedule where you feel confident you can focus and be consistent.

If you’ve carved out the time in your schedule and you’re ready to pull the trigger, consider adding a product like THREE’s Purifí to support your cleanse. Purifí is designed to support the body’s natural purification processes. During a total body detox cleanse, Purifí is used to support detoxification, healthy weight, and nutrient absorption.

When is The Right Time to Start a Full Body Cleanse?

Your body is a great communicator, and it will cue you when it's time to rest and reset. If you are experiencing the following, it may be time to consider a full body cleanse:

  • Inability to maintain focus
  • Feeling sluggish
  • Dull-looking skin
  • Digestive discomfort

All of the above are common signs that your body may be struggling to process toxins efficiently. When these symptoms become persistent and tend to stick around, it’s often a sign that your body systems are overworked or out of balance, or both!

But if you aren’t experiencing these, are there still times when it’s appropriate to do a full body detox and cleanse? Absolutely! There are many times when a detox for the full body makes practical sense: after travel, after periods of indulgence, or after the holidays. Extended periods of disrupted sleep, eating patterns, or exercise can create a buildup that leaves you feeling sluggish or off-center. In these situations, a cleanse can serve as a rest point–helping your body re-establish healthier rhythms.

Starting a cleanse should always be a deliberate, time-bound choice. Choosing a clear start and end date allows you to focus and commit with intention. When cleansing is planned and purposeful, it becomes a healthy reset that supports your body’s natural processes of restoring balance rather than adding another stressor to an already full routine.

How to Align a Full Body Cleanse With Your Routine

Full body cleanses always work best when paired with lifestyle or nutrition changes that support, rather than work against, your cleanse. Making lifestyle choices like getting more movement, transitioning to eating whole foods, focusing on regular hydration, or cutting out sugar can all create an environment where a full-body cleanse can do its best work without being ambushed by habits that undermine its cleansing work. 

If you find it hard to work a cleanse in with your schedule, consider starting it when the seasons change. Seasonal changes are often considered natural breaks and can be wonderful times to begin a cleanse. The transition between seasons–especially into spring or after the busy holiday period–can make it easier to adjust eating habits, re-establish routines, and commit to healthier patterns. These natural transitions feel less forced and align with typical changes in lifestyle routines and can feel very natural, leading to increased consistency and follow-through.

Having a clearly defined start and end date is another key factor in a successfully navigated full body cleanse. A set timeframe provides structure, keeps motivation high, and helps prevent burnout or overuse. It turns the cleanse into a focused reset rather than an ongoing obligation. A full body detox is not meant for regular use–it should be used as a temporary, intentional tool designed to support your body during a specific reset, not something you rely on indefinitely.

Planning Your Full Body Cleanse with Purifí

It supports toxin removal with its advanced blend of cleansing herbs and fulvic acid, while working at the cellular level to support the body’s natural elimination organs by removing harmful toxins and pollutants. Gentle enough for daily use, Purifí fits seamlessly into a well-planned cleanse without feeling harsh or overwhelming.

title: The Role of Probiotics and Your Digestion
description: Discover how probiotics support digestion and gut health.
author: Three
html:
Modern life moves fast. Processed foods, rushed meals, chronic stress, late nights, and endless caffeine can quietly disrupt the delicate bacterial balance of your digestive ecosystem.

Digestion is shaped by our daily habits: the quality of the foods we eat, how we sleep, and the stress we feel. These daily habits all affect whether our bodies receive and absorb the nutrients they need to function smoothly. If your daily lifestyle is affecting your digestion, you may find yourself on the receiving end of bloating, fatigue, or discomfort. This is your body’s way of letting you know that your digestive system needs attention.

Probiotics can play a big role in regulating your digestive system, and the link between probiotics and digestion is often overlooked. When paired with balanced nutrition, probiotics can help your digestive system move things along comfortably and efficiently by supporting the beneficial bacteria that naturally live in your gut.

If your gut needs a little TLC, Vitalité is the perfect supplement. Using cellular absorption technology, Vitalité delivers the essential nutrients your body needs to perform at its best every day directly to your cells.

How Your Diet and Lifestyle Affect Digestion

Inside your digestive system lives a bustling community of gut bacteria that helps your body break down food, absorb nutrients, and keep everything running smoothly. When this inner ecosystem–often referred to as your microbiome–is in balance, the state of your digestive system never crosses your mind, as it typically operates quietly in the background. Eating whole foods, consistent meals, and moving your body are all mindful habits that support your microbiome, allowing the beneficial bacteria that live in your gut to flourish.

Highly processed foods, skipped or irregular meals, chronic stress, and limited dietary variety can throw your gut bacteria off balance. Modern diets often lack the naturally fermented foods and fiber-rich plants that feed and support a healthy gut microbiome. To support gut health, dietary experts suggest incorporating foods like yogurt, kefir, sauerkraut, kimchi, and miso as good sources of natural probiotics, along with fiber-rich vegetables, fruits, legumes, whole grains, nuts, and seeds.

What you eat matters a great deal. But don’t overlook the impact that eating regular meals, staying hydrated, managing stress, and prioritizing sleep can have on maintaining a healthy gut microbiome. Your digestive system is a “system” afterall, which means that a group of connected parts are working in harmony to achieve a specific function, which in this case refers to a healthy digestion that goes unnoticed. When you treat your digestive system with care, you create an environment where beneficial bacteria can grow and do their best work. When your gut is balanced, it works behind the scenes–quietly, consistently, and powerfully.

The Role of Probiotics in Digestion

Probiotics are live microorganisms that live in your gut and support digestion. They are a natural part of a healthy gut–think of them as daily helpers that encourage digestion to run more smoothly. Probiotics help create an environment where beneficial bacteria (nature’s decomposers) can thrive. When digestion feels supported, meals feel lighter, routines feel steadier, and the body can focus its energy where it’s needed most.

Consistency is key when it comes to probiotic support. Taking probiotics regularly helps maintain a steady presence of beneficial bacteria, reinforcing balance day after day. That said, probiotics don’t work in isolation. They fit best into a broader gut health lifestyle that includes a variety of fiber-rich foods, hydration, regular meals, movement, rest, and stress management. Together, these habits create a supportive foundation where probiotics can do their best work, contributing to a digestive rhythm that feels sustainable, natural, and supportive over the long term.

title: The Best Liquid Collagen Is Also the Most Absorbable
description: Discover why liquid collagen offers superior bioavailability.
author: Three
html:
Although marketing might claim otherwise, when it comes to collagen supplements, they are all broken down and absorbed through the same fundamental biological process. However, what can set collagen supplements apart is the way collagen is formulated (powders, capsules, or liquids) and its bioavailability (how quickly the body can absorb and use it).

Many people dial in on the serving size or frequency, but if you want the absolute most out of your collagen supplement, you need to focus on formulation (ingredients and formulation) and bioavailability–it's truly what counts.

Collagen works best when your body can efficiently absorb and use it. Compared to powders or capsules that must first dissolve in the stomach and lose some of their potency in the process, liquid collagen can move more effectively through digestion and into absorption because it’s already in liquid form. Most high-quality liquid collagens are also hydrolyzed (broken down into smaller peptides) and are more easily absorbed. It’s these peptides that your body uses to support youthful-looking skin, hair, and nails.

On the hunt for the best liquid collagen on the market? Collagène’s thoughtfully designed liquid format ensures that the benefits of premium ingredients aren’t lost or diluted during digestion, leading to faster absorption and better utilization.

Why Collagen Format Matters for Absorption

We’re fond of saying that you can give the body the most powerful nutrients on the planet, but unless they are absorbed into the cell, they are of no benefit. When it comes to collagen, the delivery method matters just as much (or more!) than the ingredients themselves. Collagen supplements are typically sold as powders, capsules, or liquids. The delivery method determines how much exposure your supplement gets to your digestive system before peptides can be absorbed and put to use.

Liquid formats jump the queue: no digestive breakdown, no powders that require mixing and clumping, and faster entry into the bloodstream. When you pair a liquid format with collagen that’s already broken down into smaller peptides (hydrolyzed collagen), you get a formula that’s primed for efficient absorption.

Hydrolyzed collagen is “pre-digested.” Native collagen is a tightly wound protein that your body can’t absorb intact, which is why it must be broken down during digestion. Hydrolysis uses enzymes to break collagen into smaller, more easily absorbable protein chains called collagen peptides. These peptides are light-weight, water-soluble, and far easier for the body to absorb through the intestinal wall and into the bloodstream.

It’s simple. Hydrolyzed liquid collagen means less work for your digestive system, quick absorption, and more support for your cells without all the mixing, clumping, and digestion that capsules and powders require.

What Makes Liquid Collagen More Bioavailable

Bioavailability measures three things: how much of the native nutrient is actually absorbed, how it is transported, and how it is used by the body. When people search for the best bioavailable collagen or liquid collagen for hair, what they’re really asking is how much native collagen is really being used to support healthier-looking skin, nails, and hair.

Liquid collagen is more bioavailable because it’s already fully dissolved and is often hydrolyzed into small peptide chains that allow it to bypass much of the digestive breakdown required by powders or capsules, allowing it to enter the bloodstream more efficiently. This leads to faster absorption and a higher percentage of collagen peptides that will actually reach the tissues that use them, like skin, hair, nails, and joints.

THREE’s Collagène supplement is formulated with hydrolyzed collagen peptides and delivered in a liquid format. This makes it highly bioavailable and efficient. Apart from that, the last thing you can do to cement good collagen uptake is consistency. Collagen supports hair, skin, and connective tissue over time, which means regular intake and reliable absorption matter far more than sporadic intake. In addition, liquid formulas make daily use easier (just grab and go!), helping the body maintain the consistent nutrient levels required for visible results.

Collagène: The Best Liquid Collagen

When we formulated Collagène, we made absorption a priority, and we made every decision about formulation and ingredients with high bioavailability in mind. With Collagène, you get hydrolyzed liquid collagen that uses only the best ingredients, so your body can absorb and utilize them efficiently at the cellular level–no guessing, no digestive breakdown bottlenecks–just powerful support for healthy-looking skin, hair, and nails. 

Collagène is designed for daily, consistent use and comes in a convenient pouch that is easy to take with you. With 5 grams of highly bioavailable marine collagen plus vitamin C, biotin, hyaluronic acid, and keratin, this liquid format is the obvious choice for anyone who prioritizes rapid absorption and maximum benefit.

Hydration is foundational to daily energy and performance. Every system in the body relies on proper fluid balance. When hydration drops, performance usually follows. Even mild dehydration can lead to:

  • Feeling fatigued, sluggish, or mentally drained

At the cellular level, water helps balance sodium and potassium, which are essential for nerve signaling and muscle contraction. Dehydration impairs communication between nerve cells. This is why energy with hydration matters. When hydration is supported first, energy feels more stable and sustained. Instead of forcing the body into overdrive, a dual action drink works with the body, supporting hydration while layering in clean, functional energy.

title: Debunking The Myths About Detox Supplements
description: Learn the truth about detox supplements. Discover common myths, how real detoxification works, and what sets Purifí’s gentle, whole-body support apart.
author: Three
html:
If you’ve ever felt unsure about detox supplements, you’re not alone. But detox doesn’t have to be confusing or extreme. By learning how your body naturally eliminates waste and how a well-designed detox supplement can gently support those systems at a cellular level, you can make more confident decisions about what your body truly needs. 

Your body already has natural elimination processes that operate continuously, primarily through the liver, kidneys, colon, lymphatic system, and skin. A high-quality detox supplement isn’t meant to replace those pathways or “force” a dramatic cleanse. Its real purpose is to support those natural systems at a cellular level so they can work more efficiently. 

That’s where cell detoxification and whole-body detoxification come in. This is how the body processes and removes everyday waste, environmental pollutants, and metabolic byproducts. A well-formulated, gentle detox supplement can nourish the organs involved, support cellular cleansing, and help maintain balance without shocking the system.

Let’s break down the biggest myths so you can make more informed choices and feel confident when evaluating a detox supplement.

Most Common Myths About Detox Supplements

Before diving into each myth, it’s important to understand that many misconceptions grow from low-quality or generic detox products that overpromise and underdeliver. Not all formulations are created equal, differences in ingredient sourcing, potency, purity, and absorption make all the difference.

Below, we’re debunking some of the most widespread (and misleading) ideas about detox supplements.

Myth #1: “All detox supplements work the same”

This misconception stems from the huge volume of detox products on the market. Many rely on basic or diluted herbal blends that offer minimal support, and many are formulated without understanding how different organs and pathways actually work together. 

A high-quality detox supplement will:

  • Use clinically relevant herbal ingredients
  • Include targeted organ support for the liver, kidneys, colon, and lymphatic system
  • Incorporate advances in absorption, such as fulvic acid or cellular transport technology
  • Provide gentle, steady support rather than an intense “flush”

Formulation matters, and it’s the difference between a product that merely sounds good and one that actually supports whole-body detoxification.

Myth #2: “Detoxing should feel intense or uncomfortable.”

Many people equate “detoxing” with discomfort because harsh cleanses and extreme diets have popularized the idea that a cleanse must feel dramatic. In truth, symptoms like fatigue, cramping, or urgency are usually signs that a product is too aggressive.

A gentle detox cleanse is far more aligned with the body’s physiology. When supported properly, your natural elimination processes don’t require strain or shock, they simply need nourishment and consistent support.

Real detox support should feel clear, balanced, and steady, not uncomfortable.

Myth #3: “You only need to detox one organ.”

The liver often gets all the detox attention, but detoxification is a multi-organ process.

  • Liver: metabolizes toxins and filters waste
  • Kidneys: remove water-soluble byproducts
  • Colon: eliminates digestive waste
  • Lymphatic system: transports cellular waste
  • Skin: releases toxins through sweat

A real detox supplement supports the entire network. Focusing on just one organ oversimplifies a complex process and limits results.

Myth #4: “Herbal cleanse capsules don’t actually do anything.”

This misunderstanding comes from cheap or poorly formulated herbal products that use low-grade ingredients without meaningful doses. But botanicals have centuries of traditional use and are widely studied today for supporting toxin removal, liver health, cellular cleansing, and antioxidant defense.

Herbs commonly used in effective detox formulations include:

  • Milk thistle
  • Dandelion root
  • Burdock
  • Turmeric
  • Chlorella
  • Ginger

When combined with smart formulation, these ingredients can help support cell cleanse detox pathways and nourish organs involved in toxin removal.

Myth #5: “You can detox your body quickly and be done.” (H3)

Detox isn’t a one-time event, it’s a daily biological function. Your body is constantly filtering and eliminating waste. A detox supplement’s role is to support that ongoing process, helping your cells and organs keep up with everyday exposures.

Short-term “intense cleanses” often miss the mark. Gentle, consistent support is far more effective.

Myth #6: “Detox supplements are unnecessary if you eat clean.” (H3)

Whole foods and a low-tox lifestyle are foundational, but they can’t completely eliminate environmental exposures or metabolic waste. Even those with excellent diets may seek:

  • Cellular support
  • Liver nourishment
  • Antioxidant reinforcement
  • Help managing modern toxin load

A great detox supplement enhances, not replaces, a healthy routine.

title: Why Skin Hydration Is the Foundation of Healthy Aging

author: Three
html:
Hydration is the foundation of every smart, healthy aging skin routine. Water helps maintain the skin's structure, flexibility and natural renewal. When skin is well-hydrated, it appears more youthful and glowing. Ignoring your hydrating skincare needs results in dehydration, and those visible effects are hard-to-miss signs of aging from fine lines to dull and tired-looking skin. 

This naturally raises the question of whether dehydrated skin makes you look older. The answer, backed by science, is yes. Without proper hydration, skin loses elasticity, is slow to recover, and it can even affect how well collagen can do its important work. Wrinkles look deeper, skin feels less firm, and dryness makes everything appear older than it is. 

By keeping your skin cells well-hydrated, you’re not just quenching thirst, you’re giving collagen the environment it needs to thrive, supporting elasticity, and creating the conditions where every serum, cream, or supplement in your hydrating skincare routine can actually deliver its full potential.

Building a Hydrating Skincare Routine for Aging Skin

True hydration starts with replenishing water in the skin, while moisturizing helps lock that water in–both are essential elements for any effective skin aging routine. If you’re looking for a simple, practical guide for making hydration part of your daily skin aging routine, follow these steps in the order listed below:

  1. Cleanser. Use a gentle cleanser that doesn’t strip away natural oils.
  2. Hydrating Serum. Use a serum rich in water-binding ingredients, such as hyaluronic acid, to plump and refresh the skin.
  3. Moisturizer. This step is really important; it will seal in the hydration.
  4. SPF products. Don’t skip this step! SPF products protect against UV damage, which is one of the biggest culprits of premature aging.

Additionally, as you go through your day, don’t be afraid to add additional hydration products–they’re not just for the morning! Products like facial mists can give a quick refresh between meetings, and lightweight serums or creams can be reapplied to areas that feel dry or tight. Drinking enough water will hydrate from within, and when coupled with topical products, will give your skin the consistent support it needs to age gracefully. 

FAQs for Youthful, Hydrated Skin

Still have questions? We’ve compiled a list of common questions people ask about hydration and its role in achieving youthful-looking skin or as a defense against unhealthy aging.

Can drinking more water improve skin aging? 

Drinking water supports overall hydration, but visible skin benefits will be modest without topical or supplemental support. Pairing good water intake with collagen supplements or hyaluronic acid serum can amplify results.

What’s the difference between hydration and moisturization in skincare?

Hydration adds water to the skin, while moisturization locks that water in and prevents loss. Layering a hydrating serum under a moisturizer is the way to get the best results.

Does dehydrated skin make you look older?

Yes! Dehydration exaggerates fine lines, dullness, and loss of elasticity. Using a facial mist or reapplying a lightweight hydrator during the day can keep skin looking plump.

What ingredients should I look for in hydrating skincare for aging skin?

Smart hydrating skincare products will include hyaluronic acid, glycerin, ceramides, peptides, and vitamin C. These ingredients are proven hydrators and support collagen.

What is the best skincare routine for youthful, hydrated skin?
